A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SoundCTM, with matching core equations, algorithms, and retained experiments. The main texts, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original AudioCaps generation experiments, feature-extractor ablations, inference measurements, and sound-intensity-control experiments, including supplementary results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and adds full-band generation, listening studies, semantic-preservation measurements, component ablations, and zero-shot bandwidth-extension results.

M1.justification: v3 adds SoundCTM-DiT-1B with a diffusion-transformer architecture, CLAP text conditioning, and a waveform VAE for 44.1 kHz generation, substantially extending v1's UNet/mel-spectrogram system. It also applies data-consistency sampling to bandwidth extension. The core distillation losses remain unchanged, and the renamed ν-sampling is algebraically equivalent to v1's ν-interpolation.

E1.justification: AudioCaps generation and intensity control are retained. v3 adds full-band 44.1 kHz generation, AudioSet and MUSDB18-HQ training for its new VAE, and zero-shot bandwidth extension from low-pass observations. The restoration task and additional audio coverage substantially broaden the empirical scope.

E2.justification: v3 adds AudioLCM to the 16 kHz comparison and evaluates Stable Audio Open and AudioLDM2-48kHz in full-band comparisons. v1's AudioLDM-Large-FT, AudioLDM2-Full-Large, and separately identified ConsistencyTTA-CLAP-FT entries disappear from the main benchmark. The DITTO-2 intensity-control rows relabel retained zT-optimization results.

E3.justification: New protocols include full-band evaluation with a reported 4,875 captions and FDopenl3, listening studies with 17 and 15 participants, and bandwidth-extension evaluation on 500 samples using a 3 kHz cutoff and LSD. DiT introduces different training and EMA settings. ConsistencyTTA uses different guidance settings, and timing evaluations move from A6000/Xeon measurements to H100/A100 measurements.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative semantic-preservation analysis, GAN-loss/memory evidence, UNet-versus-DiT comparisons, DSM-loss ablations, and extended feature-loss and guidance sensitivity studies (Appendices C and E). Conversely, v1's partial-versus-entire feature-extractor comparison and some combined optimization/guidance analyses are removed. These changes substantially revise the questions investigated beyond headline performance.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty estimates. v3 introduces 95% confidence intervals for both listening studies (Tables 4 and 9) and means with across-sample standard deviations for semantic-preservation scores (Table 7). Neither version establishes repeated training runs or training-seed variability.

E6.justification: The main 16 kHz SoundCTM scores remain unchanged between v1 Table 6 and v3 Table 2, including one-step FAD 2.08 and sixteen-step FAD 1.38. Substantial new results include full-band sixteen-step FDopenl3 72.24, listening scores, semantic-preservation measurements, and eight-step bandwidth-extension LSD 12.9. Some older control and timing results disappear; revised ConsistencyTTA scores involve changed guidance settings.

T1.justification: The substantive PF-ODE, consistency objective, teacher-feature distance, and guidance mathematics are retained. ν-sampling rewrites the existing interpolation equivalently. Expanded consistency-model background and EDM parameterization explain existing machinery; no new theorem, proof, or substantive theoretical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes fast one-step/multi-step generation and newly proposed training-free control frameworks. v3 makes semantic-preserving trial-and-refinement and the first large-scale full-band T2S distillation model central contributions. Section 4.3 explicitly narrows intensity control to a potential application rather than a new competing control method.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges that CD-based models can improve quality through multiple steps and locates their limitation in semantic preservation, refining v1's broader speed/quality criticism. New interpretations address DSM's multi-step benefits and differences between objective and listening evaluations. Appendices C and F discuss the remaining one-step teacher gap and limitations when teacher and student training distributions differ.

D1.justification: v3 adds source-code and audio-sample links, a reproducibility statement, and extensive waveform-VAE/DiT implementation details, including architecture, loss weights, training data, batch size, and training duration. It also clarifies embeddings and teacher parameterization for the retained model. However, v1's explicit 18K/30K training-iteration distinction for the 16 kHz experiments is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially revised around AudioLCM, full-band Stable Audio models, and latent/adversarial diffusion distillation. Appendix A newly distinguishes teacher features for CTM loss from discriminator-based and LatentLPIPS approaches. The optimization-based control procedure is reattributed to DITTO-2, while the AudioGen/MAGNeT discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around full-band generation and semantic-preserving refinement. CTM limitations move into appendix discussions, sampling gains a dedicated subsection, and control becomes an experimental application. The appendices are reorganized into related work, technical discussions, implementation details, additional experiments, and limitations.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the opening performance scatterplot with a workflow-oriented spectrogram/listening-score figure, rearranges the teacher-feature schematic, and adds numerous spectrogram comparisons, heatmaps, evaluation tables, and listening-interface screenshots. Retained intensity plots are relabeled and consolidated from four figures into two, dropping the one-step optimization panels. The conference layout also changes throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central promises. Whereas v1 relies on objective 16 kHz scores, v3 adds full-band validation, listening studies with confidence intervals, direct semantic-preservation measurements, and component ablations (Tables 3–4 and 7–13). These address important gaps in perceptual validation and support for refinement across sampling steps. More precise positioning and explicit limitations also help. Removed exploratory analyses and omitted legacy training-iteration counts reduce some detail, but the central evidential gains outweigh those losses.
